text:
Mikko Rantanen's night in Vegas on Nov. 17 is the one Dallas will remember: four points, and, as the Dallas Hoops Journal put it, he "Checked The Clock, Threw It On Net And Tied It With 5 Seconds Left." The Stars won 4-3, and they have barely lost since. He ranks 17th in the league in wins added, his goals landing when games swing.

The finishing is running hot. He has 10 goals on 6.2 expected (expected goals: the quality of his chances), shooting 23% after 16% last season, and Dallas has scored 8.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice. That kind of number rarely holds. His playmaking is intact: 18 assists, 12 power-play points, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries. At 30, a Stanley Cup winner with Colorado in 2022, he is still making the plays that don't depend on luck; The Athletic's Jesse Granger described him dancing "around a defender at the blue line" to set up a goal in Vegas. The goals are running ahead of him. The playmaking is the part to trust.
headline: Rantanen keeps finding the clock in Dallas
